Package hadur2.core.ledger

Class EnergyLedger

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.ledger.EnergyLedger
public final class EnergyLedger extends Object
Explains the enemy's energy changes between two scans, so that only a drop the enemy spent on a bullet becomes a wave (WAVE-1, WAVE-2).

Between scans the enemy's energy moves for four reasons besides firing: our bullets hit it, its bullets hit us (it gains 3 × power), it hits a wall, or the robots collide. The events for the first two and the last arrive in the same tick as the scan that shows their effect, and are processed before it, so they are held here until the scan. Wall hits have no event; they show as the enemy's velocity dropping to zero faster than it can brake, next to a wall.

1.20 read every raw drop in [0.1, 3.0] as a shot. Drops the ledger explains away are counted as phantom waves; drops it recovers from outside that range as hidden shots.

Where it sits in the tick: HadurCore feeds it ourBulletHit(double), enemyBulletHitUs(double) and robotsCollided() from the tick's events, then calls scan(long, double, double, double, double) with the duel opponent's scan. A EnergyLedger.Reading whose EnergyLedger.Reading.shot() is true becomes the enemy's firing wave at power EnergyLedger.Reading.corrected(), and also heats the enemy's gun in the END-1 estimate. newRound() clears it at each round's start and when a melee ends and the duel's tracking starts again.

The sign convention is the drop's: a positive raw or corrected value is energy the enemy lost. All energies are in the engine's energy points. The ledger may depend only on the engine's rules (Rules), so nothing the gun or the movement thinks can change which drops become waves (ArchitectureTest.ledgerIsLeaf). It holds a fixed handful of fields, so nothing in it grows over a battle.

    • scan

      public EnergyLedger.Reading scan(long time, double energy, double velocity, double x, double y)
      Reads the enemy's energy from a scan at time. The enemy is at (x, y) moving at velocity.

      The drop since the last scan is corrected in this order (WAVE-1): our bullets' damage and collision damage are taken off it, the enemy's refund for hitting us is added back to it, and then any wall damage is taken off. What is left is a shot only if it lies in [0.1, 3.0] (WAVE-2). The held corrections are cleared either way, so each applies to one scan only.

      Parameters:
      time - the scan's tick
      energy - the enemy's energy
      velocity - the enemy's velocity, in px/tick (signed)
      x - the enemy's x, in px
      y - the enemy's y, in px
      Returns:
      the reading; Reading.FIRST (no shot) for a round's first scan

    • wallDamage

      double wallDamage(double unexplained, double previousVelocity, double velocity, double x, double y, long elapsed)
      Damage from a wall hit since the last scan, elapsed ticks ago, or 0. unexplained is the drop left after the other corrections.

      A robot brakes by at most 2 per tick, so stopping dead next to a wall means it hit the wall unless it could have braked in the time since the last scan. The engine applies each tick's acceleration before it checks walls, so the speed at impact is anywhere from elapsed faster to 2 × elapsed slower than last scanned, and the damage differs by 0.5 per step. Energy alone can't always say which, so, in order:

      1. if the enemy is not stopped now, was already stopped at the last scan, or is not within WALL_MARGIN of a wall, there was no wall hit;
      2. if it could have braked to a stop legally over a scan gap (more than one tick), no wall hit is assumed, even if a wall hit would explain the drop;
      3. a speed whose damage explains the whole drop is taken (no shot): that step is far likelier than a shot of exactly that power fired as the enemy struck the wall;
      4. if it could have braked in the single tick (it was doing 2 px/tick or less), no wall hit is assumed;
      5. otherwise the speed nearest the scanned one that leaves a legal bullet power is taken, so a shot fired at the wall still becomes a wave, if possibly 0.5 off;
      6. failing all that, the damage at the scanned speed is taken.

    • impactSpeeds

      static double[] impactSpeeds(double speed, long elapsed)
      Speeds the enemy could have struck the wall at, nearest the scanned speed first: elapsed ticks of acceleration by 1 or braking by 2 each.

      The candidates go in 1 px/tick steps (each step is 0.5 of wall damage): the scanned speed, then one faster and one slower, then two of each, and so on. Faster speeds stop at 8 px/tick (the cap can repeat 8), and slower ones stop above 0, since a robot travelling at 0 does no damage. At most 3 × elapsed + 1 speeds.

      Parameters:
      speed - the speed at the last scan, in px/tick, not negative
      elapsed - ticks since the last scan, at least 1
      Returns:
      the candidate impact speeds, in px/tick, nearest speed first
